name: Spyderco
description: Golden, Colorado knife maker known for the round thumb hole, leaf-shaped blades and the Compression Lock.

name: Benchmade
description: Oregon knife maker best known for the AXIS lock and the Bugout and Griptilian lines.

name: Civivi
description: Budget-to-midrange brand from WE Knife, known for value folders such as the Elementum.

name: QSP
description: Value-focused Chinese brand; the Penguin is its best-known design.

name: Kershaw
description: Oregon brand of KAI USA making assisted-opening and budget-to-midrange folders.

name: Zero Tolerance
description: KAI USA's premium brand of hard-use folders, made in Oregon.

name: Chris Reeve Knives
description: Boise, Idaho maker of the Sebenza, the integral-lock titanium folder.

name: Hogue
description: California grips maker whose knife line includes the Deka with the ABLE Lock.

name: Buck
description: Idaho maker of the Buck 110 Folding Hunter, made since 1963.

name: Microtech
description: North Carolina maker best known for its Ultratech and UTX out-the-front automatics, now built with Böhler M390MK blades.

name: WE Knife
description: Yangjiang-based premium brand (parent of Civivi) producing titanium-handled folders in M390 and CPM 20CV.

name: Demko
description: Andrew Demko's Pennsylvania company, maker of the Shark Lock AD20.5 series, with production knives manufactured in Taiwan.

name: Fällkniven
description: Boden-based Swedish company whose F1 pilot survival knife has been issued to the Swedish Air Force since 1995.

name: Pro-Tech
description: Santa Fe Springs, California maker of American-made automatic knives such as the Godfather, Malibu and TR-series.

name: Cold Steel
description: Ventura, California-based maker of hard-use fixed blades, folders and swords, known for the Tri-Ad lock and the SRK and Trail Master lines.

name: Böker
description: Solingen cutlery house founded in 1869 whose Böker Germany line is made in Solingen; Böker Plus and Magnum are imported sub-brands.

name: Böker Plus
description: Böker's value line, designed in Solingen and produced outside Germany (mostly Asia), covering designer-collaboration folders and fixed blades.

name: Fox Knives
description: Maniago-based cutler (Oreste Frati S.r.l.) known for Italian-made folders, karambits and tactical knives, many in Böhler N690Co.

name: Rockstead
description: Sakai, Osaka maker of mirror-polished, convex-ground high-end folders built around ZDP-189 and other Japanese super steels.

name: ESEE
description: Idaho-based maker of 1095 carbon steel survival and bushcraft fixed blades backed by an unconditional lifetime warranty.

name: Ontario Knife Company
description: Long-running US knife maker (RAT folders, Air Force Survival Knife) whose RAT series is produced in Taiwan.

name: SOG
description: Oregon-based brand founded in 1986 around the SEAL and SEAL Pup fixed blades, now making folders, fixed blades and multi-tools.

name: CRKT
description: Columbia River Knife & Tool, an Oregon company producing designer-collaboration folders and fixed blades, mostly made in Taiwan and China.

name: Bradford Knives
description: Small US maker best known for the Guardian series of compact fixed blades offered in a range of steels.

name: Winkler Knives
description: Boone, North Carolina shop founded by bladesmith Daniel Winkler, making 80CrV2 fixed blades for military and outdoor use.

name: Shun
description: Kai's premium kitchen knife brand, handcrafted in Seki City with VG-MAX, SG2 and Dual Core blades.

name: Miyabi
description: Zwilling's Seki-made Japanese kitchen knife brand, built around SG2 (MC63) and FC61 powder-steel cores.

name: Sukenari
description: Toyama Prefecture kitchen knife maker known for working with hard powder steels such as HAP40 and ZDP-189.

name: Hatsukokoro
description: Japanese kitchen knife brand that commissions blades from workshops in Seki, Tosa and Sanjo in a range of carbon and high-speed steels.

name: Yoshikane
description: Sanjo City hammon workshop known for thin, hammer-forged stainless-clad White #2 and SKD gyutos.

name: Masamoto
description: Tokyo knife maker founded in the 1800s whose KS-series White #2 gyuto is a benchmark among professional chefs.

name: Sakai Takayuki
description: Sakai, Osaka cutlery house (Aoki Hamono) producing hand-forged traditional and modern kitchen knives.
